---
title: "Talks & Reach"
description: "Douglas Fritz's talks and posters, newest first, with where each was hosted, its research pillars and links to any public event page, slides, poster or recording."
# Card titles are not sections: no "#" anchor links on them.
anchor-sections: false
# The archive script runs before the map script (modules run in document
# order); the map asks it for the current records (see js/archive-filters.js).
# The map's libraries are self-hosted (assets/vendor/, npm run vendor:map);
# js/talks-map.js loads their scripts itself, so that a missing library only
# disables the map.
include-in-header:
  text: |
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="../assets/vendor/leaflet/leaflet.css">
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="../assets/vendor/leaflet.markercluster/MarkerCluster.css">
    <script type="module" src="../js/archive-filters.js"></script>
    <script type="module" src="../js/talks-map.js"></script>
listing:
  id: talks
  contents: ../data/generated/talks.yml
  template: ../templates/talk.ejs.md
  # Keep the generated order (date, newest first, then title and key) and
  # render every record: no Quarto sorting, paging, filtering, categories or
  # feed. js/archive-filters.js does the filtering.
  sort: false
  page-size: 100000
  filter-ui: false
  sort-ui: false
  categories: false
  feed: false
  # Quarto reformats the `date` field of listing items; this keeps it ISO
  # (YYYY-MM-DD), and the template writes the readable date itself.
  date-format: "YYYY-MM-DD"
  template-params:
    # Canonical pillar order (R/config.R); sets each pillar's number.
    pillars:
      - "Infectious-disease biology, evolution and environment"
      - "Quantitative and experimental biomedical discovery"
      - "Clinical translation and health-system improvement"
      - "Climate and planetary health in medicine"
    # Canonical event scopes, smallest first (R/config.R).
    scopes:
      - "local"
      - "regional"
      - "national"
      - "international"
---

On this page, *reach* means the documented places and institutions that hosted these talks, and the public materials that go with them. An in-person talk is listed at its event location. A virtual talk is listed at its host's location and marked **Virtual**: it does not imply travel. The summary counts presentations, countries, cities, hosts, public links and years only. It makes no claim about audience size or impact.
